subject: Fleet Sculptor: sizing intake for LumenPay pilot
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit@lumenpay.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Fleet Sculptor: sizing intake for LumenPay pilot

Hi Amit —

Thanks for the call earlier. To make sure we size Dedicated correctly for your pilot, could you share a short traffic snapshot and a couple of clarifying answers below? No need for long exports — a CSV with a few sample minutes is perfect.

Quick ask:
- Typical QPS during a normal minute and an example peak minute (UTC timestamps helps)
- Average prompt token length and average response token length (or ranges)
- Percent of requests that are chat-like (multi-turn session) vs. stateless single prompts
- % of requests that require streaming (low-latency partial output)
- Expected concurrency (active sessions) at peak and baseline
- Any SLAs (P99 latency targets) or cost targets we should optimize for

If easier, attach a 10–20 row sample CSV with timestamp, request_type, prompt_tokens, response_tokens, session_id (optional). I can loop Marissa/Karthik in for the sizing math once we have that.

Thanks — looking forward to the sample.

— Jonas
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: fleet-sculptor-intake-template.csv (csv)]

Jonas —

Appreciate the checklist. I attached a short sample export from last Thursday (10 rows) and included a couple of answers inline. Hope this helps. Happy to hop on another quick call if helpful.

Sample highlights (from sample CSV):
- Baseline QPS: 2.1 (sustained)
- Peak sample minute QPS: 18.7 (10:23:00 UTC)
- Prompt tokens (mean): 92
- Response tokens (mean): 240
- Chat sessions: ~48% of requests (session_id present)
- Streaming: ~30% (mostly for user-facing assistant responses)
- Expected pilot concurrency: 40–60 active sessions (user sessions that may issue turns)
- SLA target: P95 <= 400 ms for interactive flows, P99 <= 1.2 s

Attached: lumenpay_traffic_sample.csv

— Amit
VP Product, LumenPay

Marissa / Karthik —

Amit sent the sample and the quick answers (attached). Highlights: peak ~19 QPS in a minute, ~48% multi-turn sessions, mean prompt 92 / response 240 tokens, ~30% streaming. SLA requests are fairly tight for interactive flows (P95 400ms).

Can you do a first-pass back-of-envelope sizing for a pilot ( ~1 month, predictable traffic, need cost-efficient but latency-focused ) and call out any immediate red flags? Please include: GPU count estimate (for our recommended instance SKUs), recommended batching strategy, whether KV cache/prefix caching will materially change the sizing, and any short notes about fallback models for cost control.

Copying Amit so he sees the timeline.

— Jonas

Subject: Re: Fleet Sculptor: sizing intake for LumenPay pilot

Hi all —

Thanks for the sample, Amit — nice and compact. First-pass sizing notes below (quick summary for the pilot). Attaching a short PDF with the worked math and assumptions.

Summary (pilot target: sustain baseline, tolerate 2x short bursts):
- Baseline token QPS estimate (tokens generated + consumed): ~ (2.1 QPS * (92+240)) ≈ 705 tokens/s baseline
- Peak-minute token QPS (using 19 QPS peak): ~ (19 * 332) ≈ 6,308 tokens/s for the minute
- Effective concurrency: pilot-session concurrency 50 active sessions ⇒ ~10–12 concurrent model generations depending on turn timing

Hardware recommendation (cost/latency tradeoff):
- Pilot cluster: 4 x A100-40GB (reserved for pilot month) with autoscale policy to add 1 additional node for sustained bursts above baseline. Rationale: preserves KV cache capacity and supports multi-turn context sizes up to 8k tokens if needed.
- If LumenPay wants lower cost/core throughput, we can propose 6 x A10G with streaming-optimized runtime but that risks higher P99s for long responses.

Batching and caching notes:
- Use small continuous batching window (~10–15 ms) for interactive flows to hit P95 target without sacrificing throughput.
- Enable per-session KV cache for chat sessions — we estimate ~25% token savings on repeated context and model warm cache that reduces average latency for subsequent turns.

Fallbacks / cost controls:
- Default route: rtx-8-bit quantized variant of the model for non-critical background jobs.
- Canary: 1–2 nodes running lower-cost model families to soak background traffic and keep peak billing in check.

Open questions / risks:
- Are there long-running sessions with >8k context? If so, memory pressure could push us to A100-80GB or split-context strategies.
- Do you expect sustained multi-hour peaks? Our recommendation assumes minute-scale bursts.

Next steps: if this looks reasonable, we’ll prepare a formal capacity proposal + estimated monthly cost for the pilot and a simple canary rollout plan. Would you like a 30-minute sizing walkthrough today or tomorrow?

— Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: fleet-sculptor-initial-notes.pdf (pdf)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-05-07T15:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fleet Sculptor: sizing intake for LumenPay pilot

Quick add — one operational note: please include the token distribution histogram if available (percentiles of response length). Our conservative sizing upsizes by ~20% when P99 token length is >600 tokens. If Amit can attach that to the Drive link, I’ll fold it into the cost model.

Also: I recommend we enable automatic fallback to a smaller model family for burst overflow rather than queueing — gives better UX for interactive apps.

— Karthik
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
